body.text: Many international patients receive dozens of conflicting quotes within hours of searching online, often from commission-paid sales coordinators rather than doctors. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), we operate as an independent, client-paid, flat-fee travel, business, and medical travel advisory run by our two founders in Türkiye—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions. Itinerary of Türkiye does not provide clinical advice or emergency medical care, and we never accept referral fees from any clinic or hospital.
Why should international patients consult at least 2–3 vetted providers before deciding?

Consulting two to three vetted providers exposes outliers in diagnosis, surgical scope, and hospital standards before you pay a deposit. A single quote gives you no baseline for realistic recovery timelines, material brands, or whether the person proposing your plan is the licensed surgeon who will actually treat you.

Public health guidance from [NaTHNaC TravelHealthPro on Travelling for Treatment](https://travelhealthpro.org.uk/factsheets/travelling-for-treatment-medical-tourism) explicitly states that patients should speak directly with the treating clinician prior to travel and never accept medical advice from a sales team, administrator, or travel agent. In Türkiye, every facility treating international patients must hold an official [International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate from the Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html), governed by the [Regulation on International Health Tourism](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-108974/regulation-on-international-health-tourism-and-tourist-health.html).
How do you compare clinical plans when one clinic recommends fewer grafts or veneers than another?

When one clinic proposes 3,200 hair grafts or 16 conservative veneers while another pitches 5,500 grafts or 24 full-coverage crowns, treat the gap as a clinical question—not a volume bargain. Ask each doctor to explain their biological reasoning, donor-area preservation, or tooth-enamel conservation directly during a video consultation.

Higher numbers on a quote sheet often mean heavier tissue removal, over-harvested donor zones, or unnecessary root damage rather than better outcomes. Compare proposals across the same objective columns before making any decision:

body.text: Why is the cheapest OR most aggressive quote rarely the safest?

The cheapest quote often cuts corners on anesthesia staffing, single-use surgical consumables, inpatient monitoring nights, or senior surgeon involvement, while the most aggressive quote may push unnecessary combined procedures to inflate revenue. Both extremes increase avoidable clinical and logistical risk when recovering thousands of miles from home.

The [CDC Yellow Book on Medical Tourism](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/health-care-abroad/medical-tourism.html) notes that inadequate infection control and rushed post-operative discharge are major contributors to complications abroad. Watch out for artificial urgency—such as "today-only" deposit discounts—and verify every provider using this pre-booking checklist:

items: Confirm Official Authorization: Verify the clinic's Ministry of Health International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate.
Meet the Treating Doctor: Require a direct consultation with the named surgeon or specialist before booking flights.
Check Hospital Infrastructure: For procedures needing general anesthesia, confirm the hospital has an on-site ICU and blood bank.
Request an Itemized Contract: Ensure hospital nights, lab work, imaging, medications, and follow-up visits are listed separately from hotel and transfer extras.
Keep Home-Doctor Input: Share the written clinical proposals with your home-country GP or specialist for an independent medical perspective.

body.text: How does ITO organize side-by-side independent comparisons?

Because Itinerary of Türkiye is paid a flat advisory fee solely by you, we have zero financial incentive to steer you toward any provider. We organize your short-list of two or three licensed facilities into a standardized, side-by-side logistics and verification matrix covering accreditation, written inclusions, stay length, and hotel proximity.

Our two founders handle appointment scheduling, translation of non-clinical logistics questions, recovery hotel alignment, and airport transfer planning so you can evaluate the medical options calmly without sales follow-up calls. Learn how our [medical travel coordination](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism) works and read [about Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about) for full details on our commission-free model.

Ready to organize a calm, commission-free visit to Türkiye? Contact [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/). Please do not share passport or ID scans, medical records, financial documents, or payment details in your first enquiry. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye choose my surgeon or tell me which medical plan is best?
faq.a: No. We organize objective verification checks and visit logistics across your shortlisted providers, but we never give clinical recommendations—you and your licensed medical team make all clinical decisions.

faq.q: Why shouldn't I use a free medical tourism agency in Türkiye?
faq.a: Free agencies are typically paid commissions by partner clinics, which can bias which clinics they show you and add hidden markups to your package price. A client-paid flat-fee advisor works solely for you.

faq.q: How can I verify whether a Turkish clinic is legally authorized to treat foreign patients?
faq.a: Ask the clinic for its Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate number and confirm it against official Ministry of Health listings.

faq.q: Is it normal to pay a deposit before meeting the surgeon in person?
faq.a: Many licensed hospitals request a modest scheduling deposit to reserve operating-room time, but you should only pay after receiving a written treatment plan, meeting the named surgeon via video, and reviewing refund terms.

faq.q: What if two vetted surgeons recommend completely different procedures?
faq.a: Ask both clinicians to explain the risks, longevity, and recovery timeline of their approach in writing, and consider reviewing both plans with an independent specialist in your home country before committing.

faq.q: Does ITO bundle hotel and flights into a clinic package?
faq.a: No. Keeping your medical contract separate from your hotel and flight bookings gives you transparent pricing and full control if your recovery schedule changes.
